newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SNIPPETS FROM THE 12TH DAY AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SNIPPETS FROM THE 12TH DAY AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Snippets from the 12th day at Wimbledon on Friday:

Quote of the day: "I'm tired of this man." Cedric Pioline's comment when asked what he thought of his opponent in Sunday's men's singles final. Pioline has not beaten world number one Pete Sampras in their seven meetings, including straight sets losses at the 1993 U.S. Open final and in last year's Wimbledon fourth round.
Stat of the day: Australian Todd Woodbridge became the first player to break top seed Pete Sampras's serve since Mikael Tillstrom of Sweden in the first round.

Sampras will join Reggie Doherty, Anthony Wilding and Rod Laver as a four times Wimbledon winner if he beats Pioline in Sunday's final. British player William Renshaw stands at the top of the all-time list with seven singles titles between 1881-1886 and 1889.

It has been 50 years since a French player has reached the men's singles final at Wimbledon. Yvon Petra became the seventh Frenchman to lift the title in 1946. French players totally dominated the grasscourt game in the 1920s, winning six titles in a row from 1924 to 1929.
